descriptions.description:
Structural Stability Science (SSS) is the scientific field concerned with structural conditions governing stability and failure under Load across admissible system descriptions. Load (L), Capacity (C), and Boundary (B) are invariant structural variables of the foundational SSS/DHFT architecture.

The Structural Identification Method (SIM) is the originating scientific identification method. Dimensional Human Field Theory (DHFT) is a distinct foundational explanatory theory within SSS. Dimensional Human Physics (DHP) and Dimensional Self Architecture (DSA) are distinct technical spines within the originating architecture. The published Method–Field–Theory Relationship (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19741205) distinguishes the roles and non-equivalence of SIM, SSS, and DHFT.

Subsequent research development: SSS also serves as the institutional scientific home for an independent mathematical research program whose November 2026 publication lineage includes order preservation under real extension, admissibility and counterexamples, Navier–Stokes investigations, adjoint observation gain, operator analysis, and observability. The mathematical publications define their own systems, assumptions, propositions, and verification status. Their placement within SSS does not establish derivation from DHFT or identify mathematical operators or parameters as DHFT invariant variables. See the Mathematical Research Program directory: https://github.com/Cara-Tonucci/Structural-Stability-Science/wiki/Mathematical-Research-Program .

Originating DOI-bearing publications remain the primary authority for scientific definitions, mathematical results, and source-specific conditions. This OSF component provides scientific-field orientation and navigation; it does not replace individual publications or change their publication dates, scope, or rights. Somatic Rising Institute (SRI) provides institutional scientific stewardship and research access.
